_comment: Machine-extracted lineage proposals. UNREVIEWED. Every entry quotes its source verbatim. Not merged into data/kg-seeds.json until a human signs off.
generated_by: agent extraction pass over shrine-corpus.json + shrine_entries/ + entries/
method: All 169 rows of the corpus were swept for lineage vocabulary (disciple/murid/khalifa/khilafat/successor/murshid/bai'at/initiation/teacher/spiritual guide/heir/gaddi/sajjada), then the 39 shrine_entries files and the entries/ drafts, surveys and web-research files. Nothing here comes from model knowledge of these saints: every proposal carries the sentence that states it. Where a relation is only implied, hedged, or the person's identity is uncertain, confidence is 0.7 and the hedge is named in notes. Candidates below 0.7 are in `rejected` with a reason rather than being included.
direction: subject -> relation -> object; "A disciple_of B" means A was the pupil of B.

proposals.subjectName: Hazrat Ali ibn Usman al-Hujwiri (Data Ganj Bakhsh)
proposals.quote: His own spiritual guide was Abu’l-Fadl Muhammad al-Khuttali, who linked him to the “sober” Sufism of the school of Junayd of Baghdad
proposals.notes: The Miran Hussain Zanjani entry names Zanjani's master as "Sheikh Abu al-Fazal Khatil" and calls Zanjani Hujwiri's senior "pir-brother" — orthographically close to this name, and consistent with a shared master, but no source in this corpus states the two names are one person. Left as two separate objects rather than merged.

proposals.quote: on the instruction of his spiritual master, Sheikh Abu al-Fazal Khatil, and is remembered to have preached in the city for some thirty-six years
proposals.notes: See note on the Hujwiri proposal: the same entry reports that Hujwiri called Zanjani his senior "pir-brother", which would imply a shared master. Not asserted here.

proposals.quote: he is remembered as a disciple of the Sufi master Bahlol (Bahlol Daryai) and as a devoted frequenter of the shrine of Data Ganj Bakhsh
proposals.notes: shrine_entries/Madho Lal Hussain.md adds an editorial note: "His pir is given as Bahlol (Bahlol Daryai) in the Shafqat Tanvir Mirza study; confirm spelling."

proposals.quote: at the hands of the master whom the shrine’s tradition remembers as Shaikh Siyustani, from whom he received training and, in time, the khilafat, the authority to guide others.
proposals.notes: Confidence lowered — the source itself hedges the master's identity ("whom the shrine's tradition remembers as").

proposals.quote: from whom he received training and, in time, the khilafat, the authority to guide others.
proposals.notes: Khilafat as authority to guide others, not as inheritance of a seat; and the master's identity is hedged in the source.

proposals.quote: His foremost successor was Mullah Shah Badakhshi, who carried on the master’s nightly practice of habs-e-dam
became the spiritual guide of Prince Dara Shikoh and, through him, of the emperor Shah Jahan’s brilliant daughter, the princess Jahanara
proposals.notes: Stated as Mullah Shah being his spiritual guide; the same entry adds "Prince Dara Shikoh, drawn through Mullah Shah into the Qadiri way". Confidence lowered because no initiation or bai'at is stated.

proposals.quote: His sister, the princess Jahanara — Shah Jahan’s best-loved daughter — was herself a disciple of Mullah Shah

proposals.subjectName: Syed Shah Jamal Uddin Naqvi Bukhari

proposals.notes: Confidence lowered — hedged as "tradition holds"; the named master is otherwise undocumented in this corpus.

proposals.subjectName: Hazrat Syed Muhammad Khair ul Deen, known as Shah Abul Muali Qadri
proposals.quote: named his uncle Dawood Bandgi Kirmani. Astonished, he returned to his uncle
proposals.notes: The relation is stated across two adjacent sentences of the same passage: the majzub names his uncle Dawood Bandgi Kirmani as the master he is searching for, and "His request for allegiance was accepted". Independently supported by the survey's own silsila answer (entries/survey_abul_muali_qadri.md, Q5): "Lineage of Hazrat Ali (R.A), Kirmani Sadaat, Affiliation with Syed Dawood Bandgi Kirmani". Object matched to the existing saint at shrine `shergarh`, which the survey itself locates ("whose shrine is in Shergarh"). Connects two shrines in the archive: darbar-abul-muali-qadri and shergarh.

proposals.quote: For advanced learning he became a disciple (*mureed*) of Hazrat Shah Sikandar, who is credited with giving him the name "Tahir Bandagi"

proposals.objectName: Hazrat Shah Niyaz Ahmad Chisti Qadri
proposals.quote: Kandan Kabila, Ahl e Sunnat, Awaz belong in past with Hazrat Ali (R.A), Baithi Hazrat Shah Niyaz Ahmad Chisti Qadri."
proposals.notes: Confidence lowered — the survey answer is reproduced verbatim in the entry precisely because its grammar is broken; the entry reads "Baithi" as bai'at but flags that resolving it further would mean guessing at the surveyor's intent. Do not upgrade without re-interviewing.

The published corpus row (tomb-of-bahaal-halim-uch-sharif) says only that the tomb was "raised in his honour by" Jahangasht and omits "his pupil" — so this relation is currently in the research file but not in the live description. shrine_entries/Bibi Jawindi (Uch Sharif).md separately calls Baha al-Halim "a teacher of the line". Connects two shrines in the archive.

A disciple and spiritual heir of Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki of Delhi
and the master of the great Nizamuddin Auliya

proposals.quote: Guru Nanak set aside his own sons in favour of a devoted disciple, Bhai Lehna, whom he renamed Angad — "of my own limb" — and installed as the second Guru
proposals.notes: Found on 30 August 2026 by scripts/data/scan-lineage-statements.mjs, which reads every lineage sentence in the corpus. One of only TWO this file's original sweep missed across 177 such sentences — that sweep's `method` claims all 169 rows, and the scan is the first check of the claim. One sentence states both relations: "a devoted disciple" and "installed as the second Guru".

proposals.quote: Guru Nanak set aside his own sons in favour of a devoted disciple, Bhai Lehna, whom he renamed Angad — "of my own limb" — and installed as the second Guru
proposals.notes: The succession half of the same sentence, as a separate edge because the corpus distinguishes them and the entry's whole point is that the two came apart here: Nanak passed the Guruship over his own sons, "founding the line of succession by spiritual merit rather than heredity". The archive's other Sikh succession, Guru Arjan Dev to Guru Hargobind, ran father to son.
